ds: Inherent-risk factors where the real owners or controllers of a customer cannot be readily identified or verified. Includes nominee arrangements, bearer instruments, layered offshore entities and mismatches between declared and observed control.

src.t: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)

cn.rt: Cross-cutting risk factor; applies across all consumer products and channels. Opaque ownership and nominee arrangements.

rat: Opaque corporate/trust ownership, nominees and layered offshore entities, often set up via professionals.

ind.cx: Ownership chain ends in an entity, trust or foundation with no natural person identified after reasonable effort.
ind.fp: Some widely held or publicly listed entities have no controlling individual.
ind.ds: Ownership or governance is opaque and no natural person who owns or controls the entity can be identified after reasonable effort.
ind.cn: Beneficial owner or controller cannot be identified

ind.cx: Registered shareholders or directors act on behalf of undisclosed principals.
ind.fp: Professional nominees are lawful when disclosed and regulated.
ind.ds: Registered directors or shareholders appear to act for undisclosed principals, serve many entities or have no real decision-making role.

ind.cx: Entity has issued, or may issue, bearer shares or warrants transferable without registration.
ind.fp: Legacy bearer shares may be immobilised or custodied under regulation.
ind.ds: Entity has issued, or may issue, bearer shares or warrants transferable without registration.

ind.cx: Several tiers of entities across secrecy or low-tax jurisdictions sit between the customer and its owners.
ind.fp: Multinational groups and fund structures can be layered for tax neutrality.
ind.ds: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.
ind.cn: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale

ind.cx: Registry, media or documents show owners different from those declared by the customer.
ind.fp: Registries lag and may be outdated.
ind.ds: Registry, media or documents show owners different from those declared by the customer.

ind.n: Trust or foundation with undisclosed parties
ind.cx: Trust, foundation or similar arrangement where settlor, protector or beneficiaries are not disclosed.
ind.fp: Discretionary trusts may have class-defined beneficiaries.
ind.ds: Trust, foundation or similar arrangement where settlor, protector or beneficiaries are not disclosed.

ind.cx: Entity has no staff, premises, operations or revenue consistent with its stated activities.
ind.fp: Start-ups, SPVs and holding companies lawfully have few operations.
ind.ds: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.
ind.cn: Shell entity with no operating footprint

ind.n: Common address or agent for many entities
ind.cx: Customer shares registered address, agent or phone with numerous unrelated companies.
ind.fp: Registered agent and virtual office addresses are very common.
ind.ds: Customer shares a registered address, mailbox, agent or phone with numerous unrelated companies, such as a mass-registration or virtual office.
ind.cn: Registered address shared by many entities

ind.cx: Powers of attorney, side letters or signatories give control to persons not in the ownership chain.
ind.fp: Family, lawyers and fiduciaries often hold legitimate powers.
ind.ds: Powers of attorney, side letters or signatories give control to persons not in the ownership chain.

ind.n: Recently incorporated entity with large flows
ind.cx: New company shows significant turnover or funding soon after formation with no track record.
ind.ds: Recently incorporated entity or group of entities with generic business descriptions shows significant turnover or purchases soon after formation.
ind.cn: Newly formed entity with vague purpose and large flows

ctl.ds: Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Prevents account opening or activity until ownership and control information is provided and verified, with refusals escalated to compliance and unresolved cases handled under a defined policy. It stops relationships starting on withheld or unresolved ownership.

Requires nominee shareholders, directors and signatories to declare their status and name the person they act for, and declines or immobilises bearer instruments. It limits the use of nominees and bearer forms to conceal the real controller.

Requires a documented commercial or legal reason for each layer of a multi-tier or cross-border structure, with specialist review and sign-off before approval. Unexplained complexity is treated as a risk driver and can lead to decline.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.

ctl.n: Trust and legal arrangement due diligence
ctl.ds: Identifies all parties to a trust or similar arrangement, including settlor, trustees, protector and beneficiaries, and reviews the governing document for unusual control or reserved powers. It makes the controlling persons behind such vehicles visible.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

Tests whether an entity has real operations such as premises, staff, stock and contracts through documents, site or virtual visits, open-source footprint and shell-risk indicators. It helps identify shell and front companies with no genuine activity.

Validates a stated address against postal or reference data, requires recent independent proof of residence or premises, and flags known mass-registration or virtual-office addresses. It supports identity assurance and helps reveal fictitious or shared addresses.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Identifies and verifies everyone holding signing, control or power-of-attorney rights over an account, and periodically reviews whether those powers remain justified. It reveals third parties who control accounts on behalf of others.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.

ctl.n: Tightened monitoring for new accounts and entities
ctl.ds: Applies lower thresholds and closer review during the first months of an account or entity and alerts on turnover far above onboarding projections. It addresses the elevated risk at the start of a relationship.
